touches.text: Owns the inspectors and gates (draft, moving from standalone): build_inspector, plan_inspector, ticket_inspector, corrosion, exemptions, rehearsal, determinism, import_sieve, and the tester (11; Q#33, Akien 2026-10-29). (Not diagnostic_inspector: it is base's, 17.3.) The code pipeline's inspectors and gates move to CodeMother; any that are not about code (if such existed) would not. (Q#31, Akien 2026-10-27)
TESTER MACHINE, CodeMother's (was the tester device, cairn/devices/tester/)

A machine under CodeMother, not its own device (Q#33, Akien 2026-10-29): "as long as builder and codemother are not the same, it's fine. codemother is not building codemother." The separation Law 8 needs is from the builder, and CodeMother is not one (10.3.1). Nothing here needs its own process in the rack: each proof run is its own process already.
Runs a proof as its own process and writes a validation record (claim, caller, date, method, verdict, evidence, falsifier, horizon).
TOOLS: base, validation_store, proof_coverage, scratch, question, proof_discovery, chain, bus_client, artifact, system_word; machines ruling, build_inspector; db client
COMMANDS: cairn test (--hollow, --seal, --exec, …) → cairn codemother test, the CLI a client of her verb
build_inspector: python sieves run after a build; reds a component that fails one (no charter, no proofs, a silent device, ...). "We find a new thing, we add a new sieve." → CodeMother (10.3.5)
Logging and diagnostics. These can be in different files, mixed in together.
The base classes all inherit from base, and so bring its logging, diagnostics and core patterns with them:
validation_store: reads and writes seals. → Tester
